paragraphs.text: Millions of people use mobile apps that cost nothing to download. Yet developers need an income, and most free apps earn money in ways that users rarely think about.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The most common method is advertising. Each time an advert is shown, the developer receives a small payment, which is why many free games interrupt play with short videos. Some apps offer to remove these adverts for a one-off fee.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Many apps also collect information about how people use them, such as which features they open and how long they stay. This data can be sold to marketing companies, which use it to decide which products to promote to particular groups of users.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: A third approach is to make the basic app free but charge for extra features. Researchers studying popular games found that a very small proportion of players, often less than two per cent, provide most of the income by making repeated purchases.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Consumer groups argue that users should be told more clearly how an app makes money. Several countries now require developers to explain what data they collect, but studies suggest that few people read these explanations before pressing accept.
paragraphs.label: E

items.prompt: a way for users to stop seeing adverts
the sale of details about how people use apps
a finding that most income comes from a small number of users
the payment a developer gets whenever an advert is displayed
evidence that people ignore information they are given

groups.instruction: Questions 1–5. The reading passage has five paragraphs, A–E. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A–E. NB You may use any letter more than once.
